hook_text: Same July morning: frost in Johannesburg, damp grass in Cape Town. The sea is the difference.
clip_script: Touch hot beach sand at noon, then step into cool water. That is the whole secret. Land heats fast and cools fast. Water heats slowly and cools slowly, because it soaks up huge amounts of energy, lets light sink deep and keeps mixing. So the sea acts like a giant storage heater for the coast. Cape Town sits right beside it: in July, nights drop to about seven degrees, and frost is rare. Johannesburg sits about five hundred kilometres inland: July nights drop to about four, with frost on the lawns, while afternoons reach about seventeen. Go to the middle of Canada or Siberia, and the gap becomes enormous: minus sixteen and minus thirty-eight in January.
visual_style: A whiteboard beach with a thermometer in the sand and one in the water, then a map with a frost crystal over Johannesburg and a wave over Cape Town.
pacing: A quick sensory open, a clear comparison, then a big zoom out.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and see how far the sea reaches.
